_: P5.4 — what MoOS promises to be fast enough for, per hardware tier. The tier comes from moos-visual-tier, already the single authority on what a machine is. Every number is an AT MOST. They were set from measurements on real machines plus headroom, and a budget nothing has ever met is a wish, not a budget: record the measurement that justifies each one in `measured`. Raising a budget to make a red row green is the one change this file exists to make visible in review.

flagship.measured: 2026-09-18 on the development station (i5-14400F, 16 cores, 15.4 GiB, RTX 2080 SUPER, 4K at 265%), all four rows: boot userspace 6.034 s, session 1.108 s, MoOS Settings cold launch 0.46-0.62 s over three runs, MoOS's own processes 2.6-2.7% of the CPU while idle (the whole machine read 8.2-9.0% with Chrome, VS Code and Steam open). The budgets are those with headroom, because a station carrying a full desktop, Mo AI's gateway and a browser is the normal case, not the quiet one.

balanced.measured: Not yet measured on a balanced machine. Derived from flagship by the ratio the visual tier already assumes between them; the first real measurement replaces these and should tighten them.

essential.measured: The Oracle A1 (seatless, llvmpipe) is the reference for this tier and has not been measured with this tool. These are deliberately loose: an essential machine is software-rendering everything, and a budget it cannot meet would just be noise on every run.

rows.boot_userspace_s: MoOS's own share of boot: systemd's `userspace` figure. Firmware, loader and kernel are excluded on purpose — MoOS cannot make a motherboard faster, and a total that includes 10 s of firmware measures the board, not the system.
rows.session_ready_s: From the user manager starting to `default.target` — login to a desktop that will answer.
rows.app_launch_s: From exec to the app's window existing, asked of KWin itself rather than guessed from a sleep.
rows.idle_busy_percent: CPU busy over five seconds with nobody touching the machine. This is the number that catches a render loop spinning behind a still screen — MoOS has shipped one before.
